issues.claim: if updating the source on every character would run the converters and validation on every keystroke?
issues.problem: The excerpts cite performance and typing-error correction as the reason for LostFocus, and the validation scenario for TextBox. They never mention converters. The hint also leans fairly close to the answer by ruling out per-keystroke updates, but it does not name LostFocus.
issues.suggestedFix: Optionally reword the hint (RU and EN) to match the documented reason: 'Which behaviour makes sense for text input if updating after every keystroke hurts performance and stops the user from backspacing to fix typos before committing?'

issues.claim: The binding engine does not poll the source. When the binding is created, it reads the property value and, if the source implements `INotifyPropertyChanged`, subscribes to the `PropertyChanged` event. ... `null` or an empty string in `PropertyName` means that all properties of the object changed.
issues.problem: The excerpt of the INotifyPropertyChanged page shows only a WinForms BindingSource sample. It does not show that the binding engine subscribes to PropertyChanged, that only the property matching the name is re-read, or that null/empty PropertyName means all properties changed. The excerpt of the MAUI data-binding page also does not show these claims. The null/empty claim in particular is not confirmed for MAUI by any provided evidence.
issues.suggestedFix: Check the claims on the INPC page remarks (null/empty PropertyName) and on the WPF data binding overview. Add a WPF link, for example https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/desktop/wpf/data/, and a MAUI binding-mode or binding-basics link that states the subscription behaviour. If MAUI handling of an empty PropertyName cannot be confirmed from a source, say 'in WPF' for that sentence.

issues.problem: This is true as far as I know, but neither fetched excerpt shows it. The cited MAUI page excerpt does not mention BindableObject.
issues.suggestedFix: Add a link to the BindableObject API page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.maui.controls.bindableobject) with a matching linkTitles entry in both locales, or remove the sentence.

issues.claim: A change of a plain CLR property made in code never reaches the screen, even though the object already holds the new value.
issues.problem: This is acceptable for a junior question. WPF can still refresh non-INPC sources through PropertyDescriptor value-changed notifications when the change goes through the binding system or TypeDescriptor, so 'never' is slightly absolute.
issues.suggestedFix: Soften to 'does not reach the screen' (RU: 'не попадёт на экран') or 'a change made directly in code is not shown'.
